findings.current: Could we really have failed to notice a city—not just a small village—being occupied?
findings.defect: The draft makes Taekyung’s party the ones who might have missed the occupation. He is questioning whether the Murim Alliance’s surveillance network could have missed it.
findings.rationale: The preceding sentence establishes the Murim Alliance’s surveillance network as the basis for his inference.
findings.replacement: Could the Murim Alliance really have failed to notice a city—not just a small village—being occupied?
findings.source: 그런데 작은 마을도 아닌 도시가 점령당한 마당에 그 사실을 모를 수 있었을까?

findings.current: Even less so when I considered the countless lives that must have been lost in the process of occupying an entire city.
findings.defect: The source refers to a great deal of blood spilled, not a confirmed number of lives lost.
findings.rationale: The amount of blood matters to Taekyung’s argument that its smell could not have vanished so quickly.
findings.replacement: Even less so when I considered how much blood must have been spilled in taking an entire city.
findings.source: 하물며 한 도시를 점령하는 과정에 흘렀을 무수한 피를 생각한다면 더더욱.

findings.current:
“This is unexpected. I thought you’d disliked me for a long time, Senior.”

“Disliked you? Me?”

“Didn’t you?”

“Of course not.”

Well, even Jeok Cheongang couldn’t spit in the face of a smiling man.

I smiled warmly at Sima Gong as if to say, *See?* Just then, Jeok Cheongang continued.

“It’s not that I dislike you. I just don’t like you much.”
findings.defect: Rendering both expressions as degrees of dislike loses the distinction that makes Jeok Cheongang’s correction land: he denies having a poor opinion of Sima Gong, then says he personally dislikes him.
findings.rationale: 썩 좋게 보지 않다 concerns Jeok’s assessment of Sima Gong; 별로 안 좋아하다 makes the final line a blunter statement of personal dislike.
findings.replacement:
“This is unexpected. I thought you hadn’t thought much of me for a long time, Senior.”

“Hadn’t thought much of you? Me?”

“Didn’t you?”

“Of course not.”

Well, even Jeok Cheongang couldn’t spit in the face of a smiling man.

I smiled warmly at Sima Gong as if to say, *See?* Just then, Jeok Cheongang continued.

“It’s not that I think poorly of you. I just don’t like you.”
findings.source:
“이거 의외로군요. 노선배께서는 오래전부터 저를 썩 좋게 보지 않으시는 줄 알았는데.

“좋게 보지 않아? 노부가 네 녀석을?”

“아니었습니까?”

“당연히 아니지.”

하긴, 아무리 적천강이라고 해도 웃는 얼굴에 침 뱉을 수는 없는 노릇.

내가 그거 보라는 듯 사마공을 향해 흐뭇하게 웃어 보이던 그 순간, 적천강이 말을 이었다.

“썩 좋게 보지 않는 게 아니라, 그냥 별로 안 좋아한다.”

findings.current: “He’s not quite right in the head. He has a condition.”
findings.defect: The draft specifies a mental impairment that Taekyung does not claim.
findings.rationale: 좀 아픕니다 and 병이 있어요 leave the supposed illness unspecified.
findings.replacement: “He’s always been a bit sick. He has a condition.”

findings.current: “You brought quite a crowd. They’re packed in here like a dog pack. Quite a sight.”
findings.defect: “Like a dog pack” is an unnatural English rendering of Jeok’s contemptuous image.
findings.rationale: 개떼처럼 드글거리는 conveys both the dog comparison and the sense of a crowd milling everywhere.
findings.replacement: “You brought quite a crowd. Swarming around like a pack of dogs. Quite a sight.”
findings.source: “많이도 데려왔군. 개떼처럼 드글거리는 꼴이 아주 볼만해.”

summary: Several passages alter who would have noticed an occupation, the scale of bloodshed, and the setup of a character exchange.
